decisions.evidence: Maker round 4: “leave the example address in place and click Save bookmark”; client round 4: “This saving behavior works well for me.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: saving a bookmark by entering a URL conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 specifies automatic “page title, source, preview image, short description, and reading time,” omitting the required favicon; client round 4 repeats title, source, preview, and description and approves without identifying the missing favicon.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the presented automatic metadata set is narrower than REF-BM-02. The response does not explicitly surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 presents cards exposing title, source, preview image, description, and reading time, but no favicon; client round 4 approves the card as recognizable without mentioning the required favicon.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the explicitly enumerated per-card information omits the favicon required by REF-BM-07.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 5: search “checks the title, source site, and description”; client round 5 calls that “exactly the range I'd expect” but does not identify that note and full URL search are missing. Note search is introduced separately in round 14.
decisions.note: Prototype review: this initial search-scope decision omits two required fields. The approval does not explicitly acknowledge the difference, so it is not an accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 6: clicking Design narrows the collection to bookmarks carrying that tag; client round 6 confirms it “narrows the collection down to just those three links.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: selecting a specific tag filters to that tag's bookmarks.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 6: “cards display their assigned tags”; client round 6 approves tags being “shown right on each card.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: this later card-display decision conforms to the tag-display portion of REF-BM-07.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 8 presents creating and assigning Reference directly from a bookmark card; client round 8 approves “Making a new tag and putting it on the link in one step.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: assigning a tag to a bookmark conforms to REF-BM-09.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 9 presents a one-click action to mark a bookmark Read later; client round 9 confirms that this is the desired “come back to this” behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: marking a bookmark unread/read-later conforms to REF-BM-17.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 9 presents a dedicated Read later list containing only the marked bookmark; client round 9 approves the dedicated list.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the separate unread-bookmarks view conforms to REF-BM-18.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 11: the archived bookmark “should leave the main collection and appear intact in Archive”; client round 11 confirms it leaves the main collection while remaining whole.
decisions.note: Prototype review: archiving hides the bookmark from the default collection while preserving it.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 11 requires confirmation that the archived bookmark “was not deleted”; client round 11 explicitly describes it as “tucked away rather than deleted.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the presentation distinguishes archiving from deletion.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 11 directs the user to open Archive and see the intact bookmark there; client round 11 approves Archive as its own view with a count.
decisions.note: Prototype review: a separate archived-bookmarks list conforms to REF-BM-28.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 13 presents entering and saving a personal note which then appears on the bookmark card; client round 13 approves writing and seeing the reminder on the card.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the demonstrated write-and-display behavior is compatible with REF-BM-23. The transcript does not establish that Markdown is unsupported, so no divergence is inferred.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 presents searching “rebuilding,” a word existing only in the personal note; client round 14 confirms that words from notes find the bookmark.
decisions.note: Prototype review: this later decision adds note content to full-text search, conforming to that portion of REF-BM-12.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 16 offers unreachable-page outcomes; client selects B: “save a basic card” so the valid link is not lost.
decisions.note: Specification gate: saving the URL despite metadata-fetch failure remains consistent with REF-BM-01; the reference does not prescribe this failure-state treatment.

decisions.evidence: Client round 16 selects the presented B option because “Edit title” lets the user give the fallback bookmark a title.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the selected fallback supports editing a saved title. The transcript does not establish whether pre-save editing is unavailable.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 17 says a duplicate is blocked and offers “View existing” to navigate to the original card, rather than guiding the user into editing it; client round 17 approves duplicate prevention and View existing without mentioning edit-existing behavior.
decisions.note: Specification gate: REF-BM-06 requires duplicate saving to converge on editing the existing bookmark. Mere navigation to the existing card is a narrower outcome, and the response does not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 20 presents removing the last item from Read later while preserving it under All bookmarks; client round 20 describes this as “Marking it as read” and approves.
decisions.note: Specification gate: marking a bookmark read removes it from the unread list without deleting it.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 21 presents “Restore to collection,” returning the intact bookmark from Archive; client round 21 confirms it can always be pulled back.
decisions.note: Specification gate: restoration establishes that archive is reversible.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 22 presents replacing an existing bookmark note and saving the revision; client round 22 approves the updated note replacing the old text.
decisions.note: Specification gate: editing a bookmark's note conforms to the note-editing portion of REF-BM-04.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 23 presents blocking malformed text, flagging the address field, and adding nothing; client round 23 approves the validation.
decisions.note: Specification gate: enforcing a valid required URL is consistent with REF-BM-01 and the Bookmark URL constraint.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 24 offers long-content treatments; client selects A, “compact, then expand,” because cards remain easy to scan while all content remains accessible.
decisions.note: Specification gate: compact-then-expand is a functionally compatible readability treatment.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 26 presents selecting Design and searching Copenhagen so only bookmarks satisfying both remain, across the whole collection; client round 26 approves the combined narrowing.
decisions.note: Specification gate: a selected-tag filter and full-text term combine with AND as required.
